entities.summary:
Liutprand of Cremona (unknown–972 CE) was a historian and diplomat who served as the bishop of Cremona in northern Italy.

























Liutprand was born in northern Italy, but his exact birthdate remains unknown. He rose to prominence as a historian and diplomat, producing works that are an important source for the politics of the 10th-century Byzantine court. His writings provide valuable insights into the Byzantine Empire's internal dynamics and its interactions with other European powers.

























His diplomatic career spanned several decades, and he played a key role in shaping the Byzantine Empire's foreign policy during the 10th century. Liutprand's diplomatic efforts were instrumental in maintaining the empire's territorial integrity and securing its borders against rival powers.

























His legacy as a historian and diplomat has endured for centuries, and his works continue to be studied by scholars today.
